narrative: The model estimated your chance of bad credit at 37.0%. Although that is below a coin-flip, it was still high enough under this lender’s decision rule to classify the application as a bad credit risk and deny it. The most influential factor was your credit history. In your case it actually pushed the assessment toward good credit, and it is worth noting that about one third of approved applicants also have critical or other credit records. The second most influential factor was the amount requested: at 2,820 DM, it was slightly below the approved average of about 3,020 DM and also pushed toward good credit. The third most influential factor was the 36-month repayment term. That is much longer than the approved average of about 19 months, and it pushed toward bad credit; a longer commitment increases uncertainty and was the main adverse factor among the top three. To improve your chances, ask the lender what specific term or conditions would make the application acceptable, consider a shorter repayment period if the monthly payment remains affordable, correct any errors in your credit records, and provide clear evidence of stable income and savings. Reapplying with a stronger, better-documented case would be sensible.
